title: PPML-Omics: A privacy-preserving federated machine learning method protects patients’ privacy in omic data
authors: Juexiao Zhou; Siyuan Chen; Yulian Wu; Haoyang Li; Bin Zhang; Longxi Zhou; Yan Hu; Zihang Xiang; Zhongxiao Li; Ningning Chen; Wenkai Han; Chencheng Xu; Di Wang; Xin Gao
summary: Differentially private, decentralised federated learning (gradients clipped, noised and shuffled across clients) applied to three omics tasks, one of which wraps ST-Net (DenseNet-121, 250 highest-mean genes, the 23-patient breast data) to predict spatial expression from H&E. At epsilon 0.01 and 0.1 the federated ST-Net had mean squared error 0.9108 and 0.9094 against 0.9083 for central training (and 0.9261 and 0.9101 for DP federated learning without shuffling); the metric is MSE, not a per-gene correlation, and the preprint text does not state the number of simulated clients.
verified_from: Crossref (published record); text read from the bioRxiv version 10.1101/2022.03.23.485485
note: Full text read is the preprint version (Science Advances version open-access status unconfirmed by Europe PMC, isOpenAccess=N); numbers above are from the preprint and may differ in the published version. PubMed 38295178. Seed; confirmed to exist and match description (Zhou et al., Sci Adv 10(5):eadh8601).

title: privateST: a feasible framework for privacy-preserving spatial transcriptomics prediction from histopathology images
authors: Hakin Kim; Miran Kim; Buhm Han
summary: Homomorphic-encryption inference for H&E-to-spatial-expression prediction: a ResNet-18 re-architected for CKKS encryption, run on 64x64 downsampled patches, so a hospital sends encrypted images to a server and decrypts the predictions. Training is ordinary and local (28,263 spots from 22 breast-cancer patients, tested on 529 spots from one patient); average PCC over 100 genes was 0.317 (RMSE 1.129) against 0.324 (1.099) for the unencrypted full-resolution model. It is private inference, not federated training, and the authors call it a feasibility demonstration with per-spot latency too high for real-time use.
note: Seed; confirmed. Not federated learning (matches the oversight description). Sci Rep 16, article 25330.

title: scFed: federated learning for cell type classification with scRNA-seq
authors: Shuang Wang; Bochen Shen; Lanting Guo; Mengqi Shang; Jinze Liu; Qi Sun; Bairong Shen
summary: scFed wraps four scRNA-seq cell-type classifiers (ACTINN, linear SVM, XGBoost, a Geneformer-type transformer) in federated learning and tests it on eight public datasets split across 2 to 20 clients. Federated global models were statistically indistinguishable from centralised ones on the intra-dataset tests and beat local models except on the smallest dataset; the transformer lagged the single-cell-specific model in the federated setting and was slow.
note: Full text retrieved to fedlearn_papers/T1; read here at abstract plus results windows only. Seed; first author Wang; Crossref year 2023 (online 13 Jan 2024), issue 25(1), article bbad507 as described. Client numbers 2-20 are from the secondary description in arXiv:2503.09649 as shown in a search snippet.

title: Harmony-based data integration for distributed single-cell multi-omics data
authors: Ruizhi Yuan; Ziqi Rong; Haoran Hu; Tianhao Liu; Shiyue Tao; Wei Chen; Lu Tang
venue: PLOS Computational Biology, vol 21, issue 9, e1013526
summary: Federated Harmony turns Harmony batch integration into an iterative federated protocol in which sites exchange only aggregate summary statistics (starting from a federated PCA), and is tested by splitting datasets back into their original batches. It integrates scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq and 10x spatial transcriptomics (three mouse-brain batches, about 20,000 spots) with results comparable to centralised Harmony; the spatial data are expression only, with no histology image.
verified_from: PLOS PDF via fetch_article_fulltext; PMC12513639; Crossref
note: Seed; first author Yuan, PLoS Comput Biol 21(9) e1013526, confirmed. Evidence that summary-statistic federation is used in single-cell and spatial omics.

title: SwarmMAP: swarm learning for decentralized cell type annotation in single cell sequencing data
authors: Oliver Lester Saldanha; Vivien Goepp; Kevin Pfeiffer; Hyojin Kim; Jie Fu Zhu; Rafael Kramann; Sikander Hayat; Jakob Nikolas Kather
venue: npj Systems Biology and Applications, vol 12, issue 1, 41
summary: SwarmMAP trains cell-type classifiers by swarm learning (peer-to-peer, blockchain-coordinated) on heart, lung and breast single-cell data from 284 donors and about 1.96 million cells, four studies per organ. Swarm models averaged an F1 of 0.907, not significantly different from models trained on pooled data (Mann-Whitney p = 0.937); for heart, local models trained on 1, 2 or 3 studies had weighted F1 0.947, 0.957 and 0.958, so more studies gave small gains, which is a data-scaling observation in omics.
verified_from: Nature PDF via fetch_article_fulltext; Crossref; PMC13031268
note: Seed; Saldanha et al., npj Syst Biol Appl 2026 (vol 12, art 41), confirmed. bioRxiv preprint 10.1101/2025.01.13.632775 is the same work (PubMed 39868099); both identifiers recorded here. Full text retrieved; abstract plus results windows read.

title: Batch effects can impair federated learning in multi-center omics studies
authors: Yuliya Burankova; Julian Klemm; Jens J. G. Lohmann; Anne Hartebrodt; Ahmad Taheri; Niklas Probul; Jan Baumbach; Olga Zolotareva
summary: fedRBE federates limma's removeBatchEffect with secure multi-party computation on the FeatureCloud platform, handling missing values and non-identical feature sets across clients; it matches centralised limma to within 3.6e-13 on simulated and real omics data. The latest arXiv version (v2) adds a study showing that uncorrected batch effects degrade federated k-means and federated random forests, a point relevant to pooling heterogeneous centres.
note: Seed; confirmed to exist. DISCREPANCY: the current arXiv title is "Batch effects can impair federated learning in multi-center omics studies"; the original v1 title was "FedRBE – a decentralized privacy-preserving federated batch effect correction tool for omics data based on limma" (seen in search results). Authors on the current page include Anne Hartebrodt, absent from the v1 list in the search snippet. Text scanned for spatial/histology content: none found. Full PDF saved to fedlearn_papers/T1 and scanned by keyword; abstract read, body not read line by line.

title: FedscGen: privacy-preserving federated batch effect correction of single-cell RNA sequencing data
authors: Mohammad Bakhtiari; Stefan Bonn; Fabian Theis; Olga Zolotareva; Jan Baumbach
summary: FedscGen federates the scGen batch-correction model with secure multi-party computation (a FeatureCloud app), including a way to add new studies. It matches scGen on kBET, NMI and other integration metrics on the human pancreas data, with mean downstream classification accuracy loss no greater than 5% on the remaining datasets.
note: Full text retrieved to fedlearn_papers/T1; read at abstract and results-snippet level.

title: scKSFD: federated distillation model with knowledge sharing for cell type classification of clinical transcriptome data
authors: Nan Sun; Mengcen Guan; Piyu Zhou; Stephen S.-T. Yau
summary: scKSFD exchanges soft-label predictions on a shared reference set instead of weights (federated distillation) for scRNA-seq cell-type classification. Across 42 clinical single-cell datasets it matched or beat centralised and federated baselines in F1, and in a multi-hospital COVID-19 case it improved on local-only training.
note: Cited PPML-Omics (forward-citation list).

title: Clifti-GPT: privacy-preserving federated fine-tuning and transferable inference of foundation models on clinical single-cell data
authors: Mohammad Bakhtiari; Maria Louise Elkjaer; Ali Oğuz Can; Fabian Theis; Mhaned Oubounyt; Jan Baumbach
summary: Clifti-GPT federates fine-tuning and zero-shot inference of the scGPT foundation model with secure multi-party computation over aggregated local statistics. Accuracy was within 4% of centralised scGPT on cell-type classification across six datasets, reached 99% of centralised performance in at most two rounds on two datasets, and lost under 2% accuracy at 30 clients.
note: Federated adaptation of a frozen-then-tuned foundation model in single-cell RNA (closest single-cell analogue to the foundation-model concept). Cites scFed and FedscGen.

title: Toward a privacy-preserving predictive foundation model of single-cell transcriptomics with federated learning and tabular modeling
authors: Jiayuan Ding; Jianhui Lin; Shiyu Jiang; Yixin Wang; Ziyang Miao; Zhaoyu Fang; Jiliang Tang; Min Li; Xiaojie Qiu
summary: Tabula is a single-cell foundation model pre-trained with federated learning and a tabular-structure objective; federated training kept performance comparable to centralised training across cell-type annotation, imputation, perturbation and integration tasks. A later arXiv version (2607.19400) adds a decentralised agent platform and a new aged-fibroblast dataset.
verified_from: Crossref; Europe PMC abstract; arXiv abs page 2607.19400
note: Full text not retrieved (bioRxiv full text not available through the tool). Updated version arXiv:2607.19400 (Jul 2026) read at abstract level.

title: Privacy-preserving integration of multiple institutional data for single-cell type identification with scPrivacy
authors: Shaoqi Chen; Bin Duan; Chenyu Zhu; Chen Tang; Shuguang Wang; Yicheng Gao; Shaliu Fu; Lixin Fan; Qiang Yang; Qi Liu
venue: Science China Life Sciences, vol 66, issue 5, 1183-1195
summary: scPrivacy trains a federated deep metric-learning model for cell-type identification across institutions with encrypted parameter aggregation, tested on 27 benchmark datasets and 15 COVID-19 patient datasets in the preprint version. It is an early federated single-cell annotation method.
note: Full text (preprint PDF) retrieved but not read in depth.

title: Flimma: a federated and privacy-aware tool for differential gene expression analysis
authors: Olga Zolotareva; Reza Nasirigerdeh; Julian Matschinske; Reihaneh Torkzadehmahani; Mohammad Bakhtiari; Tobias Frisch; Julian Späth; David B. Blumenthal; Amir Abbasinejad; Paolo Tieri; Georgios Kaissis; Daniel Rückert; Nina K. Wenke; Markus List; Jan Baumbach
summary: Flimma runs limma-voom differential expression in a federated way so that patient-level transcriptomes stay at their sites. Its results are identical to limma-voom on the aggregated data, unlike meta-analysis, which loses accuracy when class labels are unevenly distributed across cohorts.
note: Example of an exact federated linear-model workflow on expression data (relevant to Q7).

title: Swarm Learning for decentralized and confidential clinical machine learning
authors: Stefanie Warnat-Herresthal; Hartmut Schultze; Krishnaprasad Lingadahalli Shastry; Sathyanarayanan Manamohan; Saikat Mukherjee; Vishesh Garg; Ravi Sarveswara; Kristian Händler; Peter Pickkers; N. Ahmad Aziz; Sofia Ktena; Florian Tran; Michael Bitzer; Stephan Ossowski; Nicolas Casadei; et al.
summary: Introduces swarm learning, a decentralised peer-to-peer scheme with a blockchain, and applies it to more than 16,400 blood transcriptomes from 127 studies plus over 95,000 chest X-rays. Swarm classifiers outperformed those trained at single sites for leukaemia, tuberculosis and COVID-19; this is the original transcriptomic use of swarm learning (classification, not expression prediction).
note: Full text retrieved but only abstract and results windows read. Listed in the oversight memory as [verify]; verified.

title: Swarm learning for decentralized artificial intelligence in cancer histopathology
authors: Oliver Lester Saldanha; Philip Quirke; Nicholas P. West; Jacqueline A. James; Maurice B. Loughrey; Heike I. Grabsch; Manuel Salto-Tellez; Elizabeth Alwers; Didem Cifci; Narmin Ghaffari Laleh; Tobias Seibel; Richard Gray; Gordon G. A. Hutchins; Hermann Brenner; Marko van Treeck; et al.
summary: Swarm learning for H&E-based prediction of BRAF mutation and microsatellite instability in colorectal cancer, trained on three cohorts (Northern Ireland, Germany, US; over 5,000 patients) and validated on UK cohorts. For BRAF in QUASAR (n=1,774) local models reached AUROC 0.707 to 0.736, a merged central model 0.757 and the swarm model 0.763; the authors also tested restricting each site to 400, 300, 200 and 100 patients as a data-efficiency analysis.
note: Seed; confirmed (Nat Med 28:1232-1239). Federated-versus-pooled comparison in computational pathology, but the target is a slide-level mutation label, not expression.

title: Federated learning for computational pathology on gigapixel whole slide images
authors: Ming Y. Lu; Richard J. Chen; Dehan Kong; Jana Lipkova; Rajendra Singh; Drew F.K. Williamson; Tiffany Y. Chen; Faisal Mahmood
summary: Federated attention-based multiple-instance learning on whole-slide images with noise added to weights, for subtype classification and survival prediction (1,184 slides for classification, 511 for survival in the arXiv version). Federated models were comparable to pooled training and beat single-site training; the text has no epsilon value, so the differential-privacy claim comes without an accounting I could find.
note: Seed; confirmed (Med Image Anal 76:102298). Read from the arXiv version; read at abstract plus results-window level. The slide counts come from a secondary web summary snippet.

title: Encrypted federated learning for secure decentralized collaboration in cancer image analysis
authors: Daniel Truhn; Soroosh Tayebi Arasteh; Oliver Lester Saldanha; Gustav Müller-Franzes; Firas Khader; Philip Quirke; Nicholas P. West; Richard Gray; Gordon G.A. Hutchins; Jacqueline A. James; Maurice B. Loughrey; Manuel Salto-Tellez; Hermann Brenner; Alexander Brobeil; Tanwei Yuan; et al.
summary: Somewhat-homomorphic encrypted federated learning (SHEFL) applied to cancer image tasks in radiology and histopathology on multicentric data. Encrypted-weight federated models outperformed local training and matched centrally trained models.
note: Preprint PDF retrieved, not read in depth.

title: Flexible and scalable federated learning with deep feature prompts for digital pathology
authors: Cong Cong; Yang Song; Antonio Di Ieva; Angela Chou; Anthony J. Gill; Enrico Coiera; Sidong Liu
summary: FedDFP shares only small learnable prompts applied to patch-level embeddings of whole-slide images, cutting communication by over 99.9% relative to standard federated learning. On TCGA-IDH, CAMELYON16 and CAMELYON17 it raised mean AUC by 0.11 to 0.13 over local-only training and up to 0.10 over the strongest federated baselines; the tasks are classification, not expression.
verified_from: Crossref; Europe PMC abstract; PDF retrieved
note: Seed; first author Cong, npj Digit Med 9:578, confirmed. Closest published design to federating a small head on pre-computed patch features; read at abstract plus results-window level. Whether the feature extractors are frozen was not checked.

title: Federated learning and differential privacy for medical image analysis
authors: Mohammed Adnan; Shivam Kalra; Jesse C. Cresswell; Graham W. Taylor; Hamid R. Tizhoosh
summary: Case study of differentially private federated learning on histopathology images, studying IID and non-IID splits and the privacy-utility trade-off. A classification study, not expression.
note: Seed (Adnan et al., Sci Rep 12:1953); confirmed. Abstract read only to the first 650 characters in this session.

title: Proportionally Fair Hospital Collaborations in Federated Learning of Histopathology Images.
authors: S. Maryam Hosseini; Milad Sikaroudi; Morteza Babaie; H. R. Tizhoosh
venue: IEEE Transactions on Medical Imaging, vol 42, issue 7, 1982-1995
summary: Prop-FFL, a federated scheme that reduces the performance gap among participating hospitals by a fairness-weighted objective, applied to histopathology images. Concerns fairness across sites rather than expression.
note: Seed; matches description (TMI 2023, 42(7):1982-1995).

title: Federated learning with hyper-network—a case study on whole slide image analysis
authors: Yanfei Lin; Haiyi Wang; Weichen Li; Jun Shen
summary: Hyper-network federated learning with attention-MIL for whole-slide image classification, with noise-injected parameters. Two classification problems; no expression targets.

title: FedWSIDD: Federated Whole Slide Image Classification via Dataset Distillation
authors: Haolong Jin; Shenglin Liu; Cong Cong; Qingmin Feng; Yongzhi Liu; Lina Huang; Yingzi Hu
summary: FedWSIDD shares distilled synthetic slides instead of model weights for federated whole-slide-image classification across centres of different compute. A classification method presented at MICCAI 2025.
verified_from: MICCAI 2025 open-access page via web search; Crossref

title: Embedding-Based Federated Data Sharing via Differentially Private Conditional VAEs
authors: Francesco Di Salvo; Hanh Huyen My Nguyen; Christian Ledig
summary: Clients extract embeddings with foundation models and jointly train a differentially private conditional VAE on the embedding distribution, so that downstream models are fitted on synthetic embeddings. A related design for federating in embedding space with DP, applied to medical-image classification, not expression.
verified_from: MICCAI 2025 open-access page via web search; Crossref
note: Closest MICCAI paper to the frozen-embedding concept.

title: Key-Embedded Privacy for Decentralized AI in Biomedical Omics
authors: Rongyu Zhang; Hongyu Dong; Gaole Dai; Ziqi Qiao; Shenli Zheng; Yuan Zhang; Aosong Cheng; Xiaowei Chi; Jincai Luo; Pin Li; Li Du; Dan Wang; Yuan Du; Xudong Xing; Jianxu Chen; et al.
summary: INFL embeds a secret key through coordinate-conditioned implicit-neural-representation modules and aggregates across heterogeneous sites; it is tested on bulk proteomics classification, single-cell perturbation regression and spatial transcriptomics and multi-omics clustering (with SpaMosaic as local learner). No histology images are used; the spatial task is clustering of expression, so it is federated learning on spatial omics but not expression prediction from H&E.
note: Full text scanned for histology/H&E/image: none beyond references.

title: Federated transfer learning with differential privacy for multi-omics survival analysis
authors: Gang Wen; Limin Li
venue: Briefings in Bioinformatics, vol 26, issue 2, bbaf166
summary: MOSAHit, a self-attention multi-omics survival model, is trained by federated transfer learning with differential privacy across institutions holding related cancers. Reported as improving survival prediction for the target cancer with limited data; not histology.

title: Federated learning for multi-omics: A performance evaluation in Parkinson’s disease
authors: Benjamin P. Danek; Mary B. Makarious; Anant Dadu; Dan Vitale; Paul Suhwan Lee; Andrew B. Singleton; Mike A. Nalls; Jimeng Sun; Faraz Faghri
summary: Simulated federated learning on multi-omics data for Parkinson's disease prediction compared with centrally trained models. Federated performance tracked central performance, with the best federated model reaching an AUC-PR of 0.876.

title: Privacy-preserving multicenter differential protein abundance analysis with FedProt
authors: Yuliya Burankova; Miriam Abele; Mohammad Bakhtiari; Christine von Toerne; Teresa K. Barth; Lisa Schweizer; Pieter Giesbertz; Johannes R. Schmidt; Stefan Kalkhof; Janina Müller-Deile; Peter A. van Veelen; Yassene Mohammed; Elke Hammer; Lis Arend; Klaudia Adamowicz; et al.
summary: FedProt performs differential protein abundance analysis across centres with additive secret sharing; evaluated on two multicentre datasets created for the study (five E. coli centres, three human serum centres). A sufficient-statistics federated workflow in proteomics.

title: Secure and federated quantitative trait loci mapping with privateQTL
authors: Yoolim Annie Choi; Yebin Kim; Peihan Miao; Tuuli Lappalainen; Gamze Gürsoy
summary: privateQTL maps eQTLs across sites with secure multi-party computation, combining expression and genotype data without sharing them. Tested on data from different studies; related to Q7 through exact federated regression on expression.

title: Federated privacy-protected meta- and mega-omics data analysis in multi-center studies with a fully open-source analytic platform
authors: Xavier Escriba-Montagut; Yannick Marcon; Augusto Anguita-Ruiz; Demetris Avraam; Jose Urquiza; Andrei S. Morgan; Rebecca C. Wilson; Paul Burton; Juan R. Gonzalez
venue: PLOS Computational Biology, vol 20, issue 12, e1012626
summary: OmicSHIELD, an open-source tool for privacy-protected federated analysis of omics data in multi-centre studies, with several built-in security mechanisms. Tooling paper.

title: NoisyFlow: differentially private optimal transport using neural networks for secure biomedical data sharing across multiple institutions
authors: Yunyang Li; Nikhil Khandekar; Skylar Wang; Varada Khanna; Julian Sanker; Mark B Gerstein
summary: NoisyFlow is a three-stage differentially private framework that aligns distributions across sites (a response to batch effects) using neural optimal transport. Addresses the point that privacy alone does not remove cross-site shift in biomedical data including single-cell.
verified_from: Crossref; Europe PMC abstract; bioRxiv preprint 10.1101/2025.01.31.635830
note: Preprint and published versions are the same work.

title: Direct prediction of genetic aberrations from pathology images in gastric cancer with swarm learning
authors: Oliver Lester Saldanha; Hannah Sophie Muti; Heike I. Grabsch; Rupert Langer; Bastian Dislich; Meike Kohlruss; Gisela Keller; Marko van Treeck; Katherine Jane Hewitt; Fiona R. Kolbinger; Gregory Patrick Veldhuizen; Peter Boor; Sebastian Foersch; Daniel Truhn; Jakob Nikolas Kather
summary: Swarm learning for MSI and EBV prediction from H&E in gastric cancer on four cohorts from Switzerland, Germany, the UK and the US, each on a separate computer. A slide-level molecular label rather than spatial expression.

title: AFEI: adaptive optimized vertical federated learning for heterogeneous multi-omics data integration
authors: Qingyong Wang; Minfan He; Longyi Guo; Hua Chai
venue: Briefings in Bioinformatics, vol 24, issue 5, bbad269
summary: AFEI is an adaptive vertical federated learning method for cancer prognosis from multi-omics data held by different institutions. Vertical (feature-partitioned) rather than horizontal federation.

title: VFLING: Vertical Federated Learning for Multi-Omics Data Integration with Graphs
authors: Xiaoli Li; Qi Li; Dedao Lu; Yue Lin; Saba Aslam; Huijun Li; Zequn Zhang; Yuxi Chen; Ruey-Song Huang; Hongyan Wu
summary: VFLING is a secure one-shot-communication vertical federated framework for multi-omics integration that exchanges graph relationships among samples. The one-message protocol is a design point shared with concept C1.

title: Federated unsupervised random forest for privacy-preserving patient stratification
authors: Bastian Pfeifer; Christel Sirocchi; Marcus D Bloice; Markus Kreuzthaler; Martin Urschler
summary: Federated unsupervised random forest for patient stratification from multi-omics data pooled across hospitals. Clustering, not prediction of expression.

title: Technical and legal aspects of federated learning in bioinformatics: applications, challenges and opportunities
authors: Daniele Malpetti; Marco Scutari; Francesco Gualdi; Jessica van Setten; Sander van der Laan; Saskia Haitjema; Aaron Mark Lee; Isabelle Hering; Francesca Mangili
summary: Review of federated learning in bioinformatics (proteomics, GWAS, single-cell, multi-omics) with legal and infrastructure challenges. Its single-cell section describes scFed as federated across 2 to 20 clients with accuracy comparable to pooling; no histology-to-expression application is described in the part I saw.
note: Preprint arXiv:2503.09649. Review; read at abstract plus search-snippet level.

title: Privacy-Enhancing Technologies in Biomedical Data Science
authors: Hyunghoon Cho; David Froelicher; Natnatee Dokmai; Anupama Nandi; Shuvom Sadhuka; Matthew M. Hong; Bonnie Berger
venue: Annual Review of Biomedical Data Science, vol 7, issue 1, 317-343
summary: Review of privacy-enhancing technologies (differential privacy, homomorphic encryption, secure multi-party computation, federated learning) and their biomedical uses. Background reference for the privacy-cost discussion.

title: A Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning Method with Homomorphic Encryption in Omics Data
authors: Yusaku Negoya; Feifei Cui; Zilong Zhang; Miao Pan; Tomoaki Ohtsuki; Aohan Li
summary: PPML-Hybrid lets clients choose homomorphic encryption or differential privacy by compute budget, building on PPML-Omics; evaluated on omics data to improve accuracy over DP-only federated learning.
note: Abstract read; full-text PDF saved but not read.

title: Privacy-preserving federated tensor decomposition of single-cell immune data: recovering multicellular programs across institutions
authors: Axel Faes; Stephanie M. van den Berg; Maryam Amir Haeri
summary: Federated tensor decomposition of donor x cell-type x gene single-cell data: sites send low-dimensional subspaces merged by stacked SVD, claimed algebraically equivalent to the centralised result up to truncation; on a 261-donor lupus atlas the federated interferon program differed from the centralised one by about zero AUC (bootstrap 95% CI -0.004 to +0.012).
note: Abstract read. Summary-statistic exactness for a decomposition; relevant to Q7.

title: FL-Sailer: Efficient and Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning for Scalable Single-Cell Epigenetic Data Analysis via Adaptive Sampling
authors: Guangyi Zhang; Yi Dai; Yiyun He; Junhao Liu
summary: FL-Sailer, a federated framework for scATAC-seq with leverage-score sampling and an invariant VAE, with a convergence guarantee; it argues scRNA-seq federated methods (scPrivacy, scFed) do not transfer to its very sparse 100K+ feature regime.
note: Abstract read.

title: FPLIER: Federated Pathway-Level Information Extractor
authors: Daniele Malpetti; Christian Berchtold; Francesco Gualdi; Marco Scutari; Laura Azzimonti; Francesca Mangili
summary: FPLIER federates PLIER pathway factorisation with secure aggregation so that updates are algebraically equivalent to pooled training while expression data stay local. Relevant as another exact-equivalence federated method on transcriptomics.
note: Abstract read.

title: Federated Learning in Genetics: Extended Analysis of Accuracy, Performance and Privacy Trade-offs
authors: Anika Hannemann; Jan Ewald; Leo Seeger; Erik Buchmann
summary: Compares federated learning on genomic and transcriptomic data (an AML blood-expression set of 12,029 samples and a single-cell brain set of 15,928 cells) for accuracy, performance and privacy trade-offs. A benchmark of federated classifiers on expression data.
note: Abstract read.

title: Simplified Swarm Learning Framework for Robust and Scalable Diagnostic Services in Cancer Histopathology
authors: Yanjie Wu; Yuhao Ji; Saiho Lee; Juniad Akram; Ali Braytee; Ali Anaissi
summary: A simplified peer-to-peer swarm-learning framework without blockchain for cancer histopathology classification, claiming performance comparable to centralised training. Classification of images; no expression.
